title: Grateful Dead Live at Danish Center on 1966-03-12

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of the March 19 1966 Acid Test captures early Dead enthusiasm with Pigpen‑fronted highlights like “You See a Broken Heart,” though listeners debate the audio, calling it either remarkable or muffled and pitched slow.
ai_review.review: The show offers a fascinating snapshot of the band’s formative stage – Pigpen dominates with bluesy numbers that many reviewers cite as standouts, while the overall playing is competent if not yet polished. Audio quality is split: several listeners praise the soundboard source as clear and simple, but at least one notes muffling, pitch issues, and missing material.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance highly (average ~4‑5 stars) while a single low rating focuses on recording flaws; weighting show quality higher yields an overall rating just above 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Some listeners describe the tape as crisp and remarkable sounding, whereas another reviewer calls it muffled, pitched slow, and incomplete; no consensus on a pristine mix.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line
poor_songs: Jam before Death Don't (did not fit the groove)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑era Acid Test set mixing blues, folk and experimental jams; praised for its simple, true feel but noted as uneven in places.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned positively for his interplay with Pigpen on “You See a Broken Heart.”
